what_it_does: Real applications built on large language models (AI text systems) are not just a single model call — they are pipelines that chain together the AI model with other processing steps such as retrieving documents, filtering results, or calling external services. Current frameworks optimize the AI model step and the non-AI steps separately, as if they were independent black boxes, which leaves latency savings on the table that are only visible when the whole pipeline is considered together. Ayo treats the entire application as a single graph of tasks (a DAG, or directed acyclic graph of dependencies) and schedules all steps jointly, so it can, for example, start processing partial model outputs in the next stage before the model has finished, or reorder non-AI work to keep the AI accelerator from sitting idle. The result is lower end-to-end response time compared to optimizing each stage in isolation.
